title: Agent testing, observability, versioning, limitations, and responsible rollout
objectives: Use Agentforce Testing Center to evaluate whether an agent selects the intended subagent and action.
Explain agent versioning so you can change a draft without taking the active version down.
Name observability surfaces Help actually lists: Testing Center results, Agent Analytics, utterance analysis, audit and feedback.
State limitations and a responsible rollout sequence; mark uncited SKUs Needs verification.
diagnostic_question: A VP wants the service agent live on Enhanced Chat tomorrow. Before reading, what tests, version, observability, and limitations would make you refuse that rollout?
definition: Agent testing is generating and running utterances—often from subagents, actions, or Knowledge—to confirm the agent selects the intended job and tool. Observability is watching those tests plus production conversations through analytics, utterance analysis, and Trust Layer audit data. Versioning lets you iterate on a draft while an active version keeps serving. Limitations include builder differences (Studio Testing Center versus legacy Setup), source types that cannot auto-generate tests, and concurrent-active-version rules. Responsible rollout means sandbox tests, a versioned activate, one cited channel, and a watch window—not a same-day production blast. ([Generate Tests from Subagents and Actions](https://help.salesforce.com/s/articleView?id=ai.agent_studio_testing_center_topics_actions.htm); [Generate Tests from Knowledge Sources](https://help.salesforce.com/s/articleView?id=ai.agent_testing_center_knowledge_sources.htm); [Agentforce release notes](https://help.salesforce.com/s/articleView?id=release-notes.rn_einstein_copilot.htm); [Design and Implement Agents](https://help.salesforce.com/s/articleView?id=ai.copilot_intro.htm))
why_it_matters: An agent that looks clever in a five-utterance demo will pick the wrong action in week two. Interviewers listen for Testing Center, versions (Help cites up to 20), and a refusal to skip monitoring. Legacy Testing Center and Studio Testing Center are not the same article.
sixty_second_explanation: Think of a theater dress rehearsal. Testing Center writes a script of cue lines from the cast list (subagents and actions) or from the prompt book (Knowledge) and checks whether the actor hits the right mark. Versions are the understudy cast: you rehearse a new version without cancelling tonight's show. Observability is the stage manager's headset log after curtain. Limitations are the fire code: some source types cannot auto-generate cues, and Agentforce (Default) has only one active version. Responsible rollout is preview night, not opening on Broadway with no rehearsal.
deeper_explanation: Studio Testing Center Help (does not apply to legacy Setup): generate test cases from subagents and actions using metadata and connected data libraries. Tests are conversations for single-utterance and multi-turn evaluation. The system drafts utterances aimed at triggering selected subagents and then confirms the agent selected the intended subagent and action. You can generate up to 200 test cases at a time. Permissions cited: Manage Agentforce Grids AND Manage Agentforce Testing. ([Generate Tests from Subagents and Actions](https://help.salesforce.com/s/articleView?id=ai.agent_studio_testing_center_topics_actions.htm))

Legacy Testing Center in Setup: when the agent is connected to a Data Library based on Knowledge or uploaded files, you can generate up to 100 question-and-answer test cases from that content. Custom retrievers or web sources are not supported for that generator. Tests draft in the agent's default language. Permissions cited: Manage AI Agents plus type-required permissions. ([Generate Tests from Knowledge Sources](https://help.salesforce.com/s/articleView?id=ai.agent_testing_center_knowledge_sources.htm))

Versioning Help: create multiple versions of an agent to iterate, test, and troubleshoot while minimizing downtime. Create a version of an active agent to change and test without taking the active version out of production, or keep a backup. You can create up to 20 versions of a single agent. Concurrently active agents vary by type; for example only one active version of Agentforce (Default). ([Agentforce release notes](https://help.salesforce.com/s/articleView?id=release-notes.rn_einstein_copilot.htm))

Observability on the Design and Implement Agents map includes Agentforce Analytics and monitoring, Agent Analytics, Agent Optimization, and Einstein Audit and Feedback Data. Release notes also describe Utterance Analysis clustering user inputs. Preview conditions in Builder let you simulate record or user context. Treat dashboard folder names that still say Copilot as transition leftovers. ([Design and Implement Agents](https://help.salesforce.com/s/articleView?id=ai.copilot_intro.htm); [Agentforce release notes](https://help.salesforce.com/s/articleView?id=release-notes.rn_einstein_copilot.htm))

Limitations to say out loud: Studio versus legacy Testing Center; 200 versus 100 generation caps in the cited articles; Knowledge generator excludes custom retrievers and web sources; channel denials from AI-002 still apply; SKUs Needs verification. Responsible rollout: sandbox, Ready index, tests, version, one channel, monitor, then widen.

interview_questions.question: How do you test, version, observe, and roll out an Agentforce agent?
interview_questions.answer_30_seconds: I generate Testing Center utterances, keep a draft version beside the active one, watch analytics and audit, and I only open one cited channel after sandbox. I name Help caps and builder splits as limitations.
interview_questions.answer_2_minutes: I start by asking Studio versus legacy. Studio: up to 200 conversation tests from subagents, checking intended job and action. Legacy: up to 100 Knowledge tests if the library type is supported. I create a version so production stays up. After activate I watch Agent Analytics and Utterance Analysis. Responsible rollout is preview night, not every channel tomorrow.
interview_questions.example: Version 3 FAQ change tested in Studio; version 2 still active; Enhanced Chat only.
follow_ups: How many versions can you keep?

interview_questions.question: You must change FAQ instructions on a live agent. Walk the versioning move.
interview_questions.answer_30_seconds: Create a new version, edit the draft, test it, then activate when ready. Do not live-edit the active version. Remember the 20-version cap and one-active-Default rule if that type applies.
interview_questions.answer_2_minutes: Help's point is minimizing downtime and risk. I treat versions like understudies. If we are at 20, I delete an old unused draft first—Needs verification of delete rules in current Builder Help. I never use versions as a substitute for source control of other metadata, but I do use them as the agent-specific safety switch.
interview_questions.example: Version 2 active on Enhanced Chat; version 3 draft for FAQ; tests pass; then switch.
follow_ups: Can two Default versions be active?

interview_questions.question: How do you choose Studio tests versus Knowledge tests?
interview_questions.answer_30_seconds: If I am on Studio, I generate from subagents and actions. If I am on legacy Setup and the library is Knowledge or files, I generate Q&A from that content. I do not use the Knowledge generator for custom retrievers or web sources.
interview_questions.answer_2_minutes: I read the 'This article applies to' table so I do not quote the wrong cap. For a refund-instruction change, subagent tests are the fit. For a new article corpus, Knowledge tests are the fit—after Ready (AI-004). I still add a few manual escalate utterances either way. Description text should not include the test count; Help says the description is focus, not configuration.
interview_questions.example: Refund subagent: Studio generator. New PDF library: wait Ready, then legacy Knowledge tests if that center exists.
follow_ups: What should you not put in the test description?
weak_answer_warnings: One generator for every library type

interview_questions.question: A VP wants WhatsApp, Slack, and web chat in production tomorrow after a fluent demo. Your answer?
interview_questions.answer_30_seconds: I refuse that as a responsible rollout. We test in sandbox, protect the active version, open one cited channel, and assign an observability owner. Extra doors are a later change.
interview_questions.answer_2_minutes: Help's map is test, deploy, monitor—not demo, blast, hope. Channel denials from IT Service Help still apply. WhatsApp on an unsupported template is a limitation, not a stretch goal. I offer a dated plan: week one web chat sandbox, week two production web, later channels after utterance analysis. SKUs stay Needs verification.
interview_questions.example: Written refusal: no WhatsApp until Enhanced Chat metrics are owned for two weeks.
follow_ups: What do you monitor in week one?
weak_answer_warnings: Agreeing because the demo was fluent

interview_questions.question: What observability will you actually look at after go-live?
interview_questions.answer_30_seconds: Agent Analytics, Utterance Analysis clusters, and Einstein Audit and Feedback Data. I also keep Testing Center regressions on the last failed jobs.
interview_questions.answer_2_minutes: I do not pretend I have a custom Datadog board unless the org built one. I use Help's monitor column. If dashboards still sit in a Copilot-named folder, I treat that as a rename leftover. I look for wrong-subagent clusters first, then toxic or injection-looking prompts with security (AI-005). I schedule a human review of escalations.
interview_questions.example: Weekly: top utterance clusters, FAQ miss rate, transfer rate.
tradeoffs: Privacy of logs vs debug need
weak_answer_warnings: We will just watch the group chat

interview_questions.question: Knowledge test generation is greyed out. Diagnose.
interview_questions.answer_30_seconds: Check that I am on the legacy article's center, that the library is Knowledge or files, that custom retriever/web is not the source, that index is Ready, and that I have Manage AI Agents.
interview_questions.answer_2_minutes: If we are on Studio, I should be using the subagent generator, not expecting the 100-case Knowledge button. If the library is web-source, Help says generation is unsupported—limitation, not a bug. I write manual tests instead. I do not rebuild production indexes to 'force' a generator.
interview_questions.example: Web-source library: Knowledge generator unavailable; 15 manual FAQ utterances added.
weak_answer_warnings: The product is broken so skip tests

interview_questions.question: How is Builder preview different from Testing Center?
interview_questions.answer_30_seconds: Preview is an interactive conversation, optionally with preview conditions. Testing Center batches generated utterances and can score intended subagent and action. I need both.
interview_questions.answer_2_minutes: Preview conditions help me simulate language or a record. They do not replace 200 targeted cases. I use preview to feel the conversation and Testing Center to catch regressions when instructions change. Neither is a load test. Neither proves Omni-Channel in production.
interview_questions.example: Preview as Spanish end user; Testing Center batch on Refund Request.
tradeoffs: Preview conditions vs real channel variables
follow_ups: What preview conditions exist for ASA?
Can you test email channel in preview?

interview_questions.question: Name three limitations you will say in an interview without being asked.
interview_questions.answer_30_seconds: Studio Testing Center is Beta in Help. Knowledge auto-tests skip custom retrievers and web sources. Agentforce (Default) has one active version. I also mention 200 versus 100 caps so I do not mix articles.
interview_questions.answer_2_minutes: Limitations are how you sound senior. I add channel denials from IT Service Help, Ready-index gates, masking caveats from AI-005, and SKUs Needs verification. I would rather under-promise a rollout than invent a 10,000-test factory Help never described. Responsible rollout is the practical expression of those limits.
interview_questions.example: Whiteboard corner: Beta, 200/100, unsupported web sources, one active Default, one-channel go-live.
follow_ups: How do you track versions against 20?
